records.title: Thacker Pass construction and the path to qualified lithium
records.scope: The Thacker Pass mine and integrated lithium-processing development in Humboldt County, Nevada; its logistics connections are dependencies, not extra projects in this count.
records.answer: Thacker Pass has a construction account, not yet a recurring qualified-output account. Its November 2026 issuer update increases the capital estimate while keeping mechanical completion and ramp-up as future targets.
records.stage: Construction reported; future completion and ramp-up targets

identity_decision.rationale: One named mine and integrated processing development, distinct from Rhyolite Ridge in Esmeralda County. The retained Nevada two-project comparison counts zero projects; neither financing instruments nor individual plant components add identities.

sections.heading: A mine and a processing system
sections.text: Thacker Pass links open-pit extraction to ore treatment and lithium-carbonate production in Humboldt County. NDEP describes crushing, acid leaching and a sulfuric-acid plant whose heat also supplies steam. That chain matters: an excavated resource is not interchangeable with finished material. The reader needs to follow both the physical conversion and the controls on waste, air and water, rather than treating the deposit alone as a usable battery supply.

sections.heading: Construction with a revised cost baseline
sections.text: Lithium Americas reported major construction continuing in its November 12 update. It described a revised Phase 1 capital estimate of US$3.83 billion including contingency, versus US$2.93 billion previously. Mechanical completion remained a late-2027 target, followed by ramp-up through 2028. The company identified craft-labor availability and installation productivity among remaining construction risks. These are management's estimates and schedule, not completion certificates. For this account, the cost revision changes the delivery baseline without turning the forecast into an observed production date.

sections.heading: Different approvals cover different objects
sections.text: NDEP records air, water and mining permits issued on February 25, 2022, including a prohibition on mining below the water table. DOE's environmental-review summary describes a different object: processing facilities and associated infrastructure, rather than development and operation of the open pit. A financing review therefore cannot stand in for a mine permit, and historical permits cannot stand in for a later compliance record. The useful question is which asset, activity and condition each instrument covers.

sections.heading: Indigenous rights remain part of the account
sections.text: Human Rights Watch and the ACLU's February 2025 investigation, based on 41 interviews conducted from September 2023 to January 2025, describes objections concerning consultation, ancestral land and access to Peehee Mu'huh. The report also records the company's response: it relied on federal permitting, continuing engagement and a community-benefits agreement with the Fort McDermitt Paiute and Shoshone Tribe. Those positions are not a single community verdict. This dossier treats the investigation as attributed rights research, not a new judicial finding, and does not equate an agreement with universal consent.

sections.heading: The receiving system extends beyond the pit
sections.text: The company's same quarterly update reports construction of a transload terminal west of Winnemucca and targets completion in 2027. That connection makes freight handling part of the delivery chain. It also makes the county profile relevant: a project can advance while housing, transport or public-service effects require separate measurement. Construction headcounts should not be converted into permanent local jobs or households without evidence about employment duration and residence.

sections.heading: What would establish usable output
sections.text: The next substantive transition is an identified plant's commissioning record, followed by dated output with a defined product specification, quantity and reporting interval. Customer qualification should identify who accepted which material and under what criteria. A repeated series would then distinguish stable delivery from a first successful batch. This is the editorial test for moving the account forward, not a statement that those future records have already been issued or that a particular customer must disclose them publicly.

next_artifacts: A dated commissioning or mechanical-completion instrument identifying the Phase 1 systems covered.
Plant-level output and quality records, with customer qualification kept separate from equipment completion.
Current environmental compliance and affected-community accounts alongside the construction schedule.

records.title: Rhyolite Ridge approvals and the investment decision still ahead
records.scope: The Rhyolite Ridge lithium-boron mine and processing development in Esmeralda County, Nevada; the proposed Tooele boron-carbide facility in Utah is outside this project identity.
records.answer: Rhyolite Ridge has federal plan approval and reported preparatory work. Ioneer's October 2026 filing still leaves the final investment decision undated, dependent on strategic partnering and refreshed project economics.
records.stage: Plan approved; final investment decision pending in the inspected issuer filing

identity_decision.rationale: One named lithium-boron development in Esmeralda County, not Thacker Pass and not the proposed Tooele facility. The Nevada comparison is a non-counting parent, so the project is added once without inheriting a sibling's construction or output evidence.

sections.heading: Approval belongs to a named Nevada project
sections.text: BLM's archived announcement identifies the Rhyolite Ridge Lithium-Boron Project in Esmeralda County and says the Record of Decision approves its plan of operations. The agency gives October 24, 2024 as the signature date; October 29 is the announcement date. Keeping those dates and that location explicit prevents an approval in one Nevada project from being attributed to the other. It also preserves the distinction between authorization of a plan and the later physical delivery of that plan.

sections.heading: Partnering has not become an investment decision
sections.text: Ioneer's October 27 filing, covering the quarter ended September 30, lists the final investment decision as TBA. It depends on the strategic-partner process and refreshed economics. July agreements with KIND and Hyundai Engineering are non-binding. The filing describes road engineering and exploration-pad work; these should not be relabelled as a completed production plant. Its roughly 36-month construction estimate is conditional on lead times and ordering, not a fixed production-start date.

sections.heading: Processing finance is not the whole mine
sections.text: DOE's January 23, 2025 decision summary defines its environmental-review scope as mine-processing facilities and associated infrastructure, excluding development and operation of the open pit. That distinction helps readers ask what a funding milestone actually enables. Mine access, processing equipment, construction commitments and product delivery are related obligations, but an instrument concerning one does not settle all the others. A processing-finance announcement should therefore be read beside the project plan and its remaining investment decision, not as an operating-output certificate.

sections.heading: Habitat protection is an operating obligation
sections.text: The Fish and Wildlife Service's December 16, 2022 final rule listed Tiehm's buckwheat as endangered and designated about 910 acres of critical habitat; it took effect January 17, 2023. The rule identifies several threats, including mineral development and roads, rather than reducing the plant's future to a single pressure. The designation is a historical regulatory fact, not evidence that subsequent mitigation has succeeded. A useful environmental account would follow survival, recruitment and habitat condition over time, with the monitoring method and reporting period attached to each result.

sections.heading: The legal account and downstream proposals stay separate
sections.text: Ioneer reports that a federal district court upheld the approval in March 2026 and that plaintiffs appealed in April. This is the company's account, not an independently retrieved appellate disposition. Its separate proposed boron-carbide facility at Tooele Army Depot is in Utah. Linking a potential downstream use may explain a development strategy; it cannot establish that Rhyolite Ridge has produced accepted material, or turn another facility's preparatory work into this mine's commissioning milestone.

sections.heading: The next transition needs a commitment and then performance
sections.text: A dated final investment decision and binding funding or delivery commitments would change the investment-stage account. Construction milestones should then identify the facilities actually covered. Production evidence would need product, quantity, quality and interval, followed by a separate customer-acceptance record where qualification is claimed. Environmental performance belongs alongside material performance. These are distinct tests: meeting a commercial milestone does not answer a habitat question, and a habitat-management activity does not establish saleable output.

next_artifacts: A dated final investment decision and binding commitments identifying the funded project scope.
Exact later judicial disposition if the legal status is updated, rather than an issuer's forecast of timing.
Project-specific construction, output, customer-acceptance and habitat-monitoring records, assessed independently.

records.title: Humboldt County housing access and the Thacker Pass receiving system
records.scope: Humboldt County, Nevada, FIPS 32013; a county-wide receiving-system account, not Humboldt County California, the whole Nevada materials corridor, or a statement of Tribal jurisdiction.
records.answer: Thacker Pass sits within a sparsely populated county whose housing and service systems need their own account. County-wide statistics describe the setting; they do not show how many project workers can be housed or how public services will perform.
records.stage: Dated county baseline; project-attributed service outcomes not established

identity_decision.rationale: A single named county with an exact Census FIPS and local administrative responsibilities. It is a distinct receiving-system unit within, not an alias for, the wider Nevada materials corridor. No town, terminal or neighborhood is added as another place in this batch, and overlapping geography is not treated as independent impact observations.

sections.heading: A county boundary and a mine boundary answer different questions
sections.text: NDEP locates Thacker Pass in Humboldt County. The project account follows a mine and processing chain; this account follows the county in which people live, travel and use services. A county boundary is useful for comparing consistently defined statistics and public responsibilities. It does not encompass every supply-chain dependency, and it must not be substituted for Indigenous ancestral lands or Tribal governmental authority. Rhyolite Ridge, in Esmeralda County, is not a second mine inside this county profile.

sections.heading: Housing numbers describe a baseline not spare capacity
sections.text: Census QuickFacts records 17,285 residents in the 2020 Census and a July 1, 2025 population estimate of 17,267 using vintage V2025. It reports 7,942 housing units for July 2025. The 2020–2024 ACS median gross rent is US$994. These measures have different periods and purposes. Total housing units are not vacant or available units, and a multiyear rent estimate is not a current asking rent. This baseline cannot support a calculation of accommodation available to a construction workforce.

sections.heading: Access and utilities depend on the particular location
sections.text: The county's undated rural guide warns that access, road maintenance and emergency response can differ substantially outside developed areas. Its services discussion also distinguishes properties connected to water or sanitation systems from those requiring other arrangements. The guide is useful for identifying questions, not for estimating current capacity. A receiving-system assessment needs the actual road, service area and parcel involved; a county total or a line on a map cannot confirm that a proposed home or worksite has reliable access and utilities.

sections.heading: Local planning has a different role from mine permitting
sections.text: Humboldt County's planning department describes responsibilities spanning site plans, subdivisions, zoning changes and conditional or special-use applications. It works with city and county building departments on zoning information and setbacks and initiates master-plan amendments. Those responsibilities make local planning relevant to accommodation and supporting development. They do not transfer NDEP's environmental decisions to the county or prove that a particular parcel is approved. The operative local record is the named application and disposition, not the existence of a planning department or update webpage.

sections.heading: Freight and employment create questions to measure
sections.text: Lithium Americas reports a transload terminal under construction west of Winnemucca, with completion targeted in 2027. It separately reports about 1,900 personnel at Thacker Pass as of September 30, 2026. Neither statement measures county-wide net employment, traffic delay or household demand. The analytical next step is to connect actual worker residence and duration, freight movements and service demand to clearly defined periods. Otherwise temporary construction activity can be mistaken for a permanent change in local population or welfare.

sections.heading: What a useful local follow-up would contain
sections.text: A stronger county account would pair dated housing availability and occupancy with the location and timing of workforce demand. It would identify funded road or utility works and then distinguish their completion from their measured service performance. Public budgets and affected residents' accounts would help show who bears costs and who receives benefits. These are proposed measurement questions, not a claim that the mine caused a specific shortage or that the county has accepted a particular service obligation.

next_artifacts: Named housing or supporting-development applications with actual decisions, locations and service arrangements.
Dated occupancy, vacancy, worker-residence and service-demand measures with comparable geographic boundaries.
Funded local infrastructure commitments followed separately by delivery and service-performance records.
